title: Fast Quantum Interconnects via Neutral Atom Ensembles
authors: Sina Zeytinoglu, Wenchao Xu, Thomas Pohl
abstract: Distributing entanglement between distant qubits is a crucial element of scalable quantum computing. Here, we describe a scalable quantum interconnect that generates remote entanglement at rates approaching those compatible with two-qubit gates of current neutral-atom quantum processors. The proposed approach exploits the strong dipole-dipole interactions between atomic Rydberg states to generate entanglement between stationary qubits and propagating photons, without the need for an optical cavity. We provide a thorough description of the optimal conditions for the developed entanglement-generation protocol for realistic experimental parameters and demonstrate that entanglement-generation rates $\gtrsim 3\times 10^5$ s$^{-1}$ can be achieved using Rydberg states of ytterbium atoms. Given the inherent scalability and design flexibility of the proposed interconnect, our results suggest a promising approach towards distributed networks based on neutral-atom quantum architectures.
summary: The paper proposes a novel, scalable quantum interconnect using neutral atom ensembles and Rydberg interactions to generate remote entanglement. By exploiting strong dipole-dipole coupling between atomic states, it achieves high entanglement generation rates ($\gtrsim 3 	imes 10^5$ s$^{-1}$) without requiring an optical cavity. This presents a promising pathway for building distributed quantum networks based on neutral atoms.
main_problem: The primary goal is developing fast and scalable quantum interconnects necessary for building distributed quantum networks.
main_result: The proposed method achieves entanglement generation rates exceeding $3 	imes 10^5$ s$^{-1}$ by leveraging strong dipole-dipole interactions in neutral atom ensembles, avoiding the need for optical cavities.
method: The analysis involves numerical simulations of qubit-photon dynamics governed by optical propagation equations in frequency space to model state-dependent photon operations.
model_or_system: The system uses neutral atom ensembles (e.g., Ytterbium) where a single qubit interacts with propagating photons via strong dipole-dipole interactions between Rydberg states, mediating entanglement generation.
key_observables: Entanglement generation rate ($\Gamma_e$), transmission spectrum ($T_0$), and conditional reflection spectrum ($R$).
important_parameters: Dipole-dipole interaction potential $V(r)$, Rabi frequencies ($\Omega_\pm$), decay rates ($\gamma_{p\pm}, \gamma_{r\pm}$), and optical depth ($O_{Db}$).
main_assumptions: The protocol relies on the ability to implement state-dependent photon operations using collective light-matter coupling in small atomic ensembles.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows entanglement generation via dipolar Rydberg interactions between atoms and photons. Figure 2 details level diagrams illustrating the coupling mechanism for ensemble and qubit atoms.
paper_structure: The paper develops the concept by first describing the physical setup, then deriving the necessary Hamiltonian/equations of motion (Eqs. 1-3), simulating the dynamics to calculate performance metrics ($\Gamma_e$), and finally analyzing scaling laws based on optical depth.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses a core challenge in quantum networking—creating fast, scalable entanglement links—by proposing an all-atomic/photonic mechanism that bypasses cavity requirements, which is highly relevant for experimental AMO physicists.
